name: com.aidoptio/aidoptio
title: Aidoptio
description: AI adoption services: EUR prices, estimates, prepared intake links, vendor evaluation plans. EN/NL.

tools.name: get_catalog
tools.description: Returns Aidoptio services (price model and amount in EUR excl. VAT, duration, deliverables), ready-to-deploy products and published articles, with canonical English and Dutch URLs. Filter by section and language; limit caps the items per section (default 50).

section.description: Return one section only. Omit for all four.

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English) or nl (Dutch). Omit to get both.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per section.

tools.name: search_articles
tools.description: Keyword search over the published Aidoptio articles (titles, excerpts, keywords and tags, English and Dutch). Returns the best matches with title, excerpt, date, category and EN/NL URLs. Please cite the article URL.

query.description: Search terms, e.g. "private eval benchmark" or "EU AI Act agents".

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English) or nl (Dutch). Omit to get both.

tools.name: get_service
tools.description: Returns the full record of one service or product: price, duration, deliverables, summary and EN/NL URLs. Accepts the catalog id (e.g. "readiness-sprint", "agentops-setup", "fractional-caio", "eu-compliant-rag") or the last part of its URL (e.g. "agentops", "interim-chief-ai-officer"). Call get_catalog with section=services to list the ids.

slug.description: Catalog id or URL slug of the service or product.

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English) or nl (Dutch). Omit to get both.

tools.name: benchmark_readiness
tools.description: Six questions about one process: is it ready for a private evaluation benchmark on your own cases? Returns a 0-100 readiness score, what is already in place, what to prepare, and the fitting first step with its starting price (EUR excl. VAT). Same rule set as the scan on aidoptio.com. A transparent heuristic, not a measurement and not a quote. Deterministic: no model is called and the answers are not stored.

process.description: Which process would you benchmark first? service = Customer service: tickets, e-mail, chat; cases = Case handling: claims, applications, dossiers; documents = Document intake and back office; sales = Sales: quotes, tenders, proposals; internal = Internal helpdesk: IT, HR, knowledge questions; undecided = Several candidates, not chosen yet.

history.description: How many historical cases with a known outcome can you pull? lt50 = Fewer than 50; 50-200 = 50 to 200; 200-1000 = 200 to 1,000; gt1000 = More than 1,000; unknown = I don't know yet.

sensitivity.description: How sensitive is the data in these cases? low = Low: mostly public or internal information; medium = Medium: customer data, can be pseudonymised; high-classified = High (health, financial, special categories), and classified; high-unclear = High, and nobody has classified it yet.

redlines.description: Are there hard red-line rules the system must never break? written = Yes, written down in policies or procedures; tacit = Yes, but they live in our experts' heads; none = Not that we know of; unsure = I'm not sure.

models.description: How do you use AI models or tools in this process today? none = Not yet; adhoc = Employees use general chat assistants ad hoc; pilot = A pilot or proof of concept with one model; production = In production, and we want to compare or switch models.

volume.description: What monthly volume do you want this process to handle? lt100 = Fewer than 100; 100-1000 = 100 to 1,000; 1000-10000 = 1,000 to 10,000; gt10000 = More than 10,000.

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: ai_act_triage
tools.description: Five questions about one AI use or agent. Returns an indicative risk tier under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (prohibited, high-risk, transparency, minimal), whether agent risk is high, the deadlines that apply, the controls to put in place and first steps, with the EUR-Lex source and the date the status was last checked. Same rule set as the triage on aidoptio.com. Indicative triage, not legal advice. Deterministic: no model is called and the answers are not stored.

domain.description: Application domain and impact on people prohibited = Manipulation, social scoring or emotion recognition at work; high = Recruitment, credit, life or health insurance, education, essential services, critical infrastructure; transparency = Chatbot or generated content facing customers or citizens; minimal = Internal knowledge search or writing assistant.

autonomy.description: Degree of autonomy of the system or agent draft = Draft proposal for an employee only; autonomous = Independently executes external actions or transactions via tools or MCP.

data.description: Data processing and origin none = No personal data; eea = Standard business data and personal data within the EEA; sensitive = Special category data or customer data outside the EEA.

role.description: Your organisation's role under the EU AI Act deployer = Deployer of existing models or tools; provider = Provider, or substantial modification or fine-tuning under your own brand.

maturity.description: Current assurance and AI literacy (Art. 4) solid = Role training, AI register, DPIA and kill switch in place; partial = Partly: policy or training, but no complete register or test; adhoc = Still ad hoc.

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: verify_ai_text
tools.description: Checks a text against the fingerprints of answers given by the AI assistant on aidoptio.com (AI Act Article 50(2) marking). Returns match (the whole text), partial (some sentences, with counts and dates), none or inactive. It only knows the Aidoptio assistant: "none" says nothing about other AI systems. The text is hashed in memory and never stored. Limit: 20 checks per hour.

text.description: The text to check, as copied.

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: plan_vendor_evaluation
tools.description: For a buyer choosing between 2 and 8 AI vendors. Returns weighted criteria (sum 100), a test plan on your own cases (typical, edge and red-line cases; red lines pass only with zero violations), data-route rules for the sensitivity you give, a preregistration (canonical JSON plus SHA-256 method hash) to freeze before the first vendor run, six questions to ask any advisor (us included), Aidoptio's own disclosure for this shortlist, and one fitting next step. The plan works without Aidoptio. Case numbers are an Aidoptio method default, not a scientific norm; a plan, not a measurement and not legal advice. Deterministic: same input, same hash. Vendor names are part of the hash and are not stored. monthly_volume is validated but does not change the plan.

use_case.description: The process the vendors are evaluated for: service (customer service), cases (case handling), documents (document intake and back office), sales, internal (internal helpdesk) or other.

vendors.description: Names of the vendors on the shortlist. Order does not matter for the hash.

data_sensitivity.description: low (public or internal), medium (customer data, can be pseudonymised), high-classified (health, financial or special categories, and classified) or high-unclear (high, not classified yet).

red_lines.description: Rules a system must never break, e.g. "Never promise a refund".

priorities.description: Weight per dimension: high, normal (default) or low.

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: verify_report
tools.description: For a client, an auditor or a later buyer who holds an Aidoptio evaluation report. Give the report number and the method hash printed in it; the tool reads the public, append-only method log, verifies the whole hash chain and answers: match, match_superseded (a logged deviation replaced the hash), hash_mismatch or unknown_report, with the freeze date, whether the first vendor run came after the freeze, the deviations and the disclosure logged with the report. Read-only; nothing is stored.

method_hash.description: SHA-256 method hash from the report: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

tools.name: get_disclosures
tools.description: Returns Aidoptio's public register of vendor relations (the content of /.well-known/disclosures.json: fees received from vendors, resale, each relation with its category, status and default rule), the six rules of the independence policy in the chosen language, and the URLs of the policy, the machine-readable register and the public method log. Relations without a public name are listed by category only and confirmed per name, in writing, in a proposal. The policy is a draft that has not been legally reviewed yet (see policy_status).

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: ai_literacy_scan
tools.description: For an organisation that wants to show what it does about AI literacy under Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Give the role groups and, optionally, your own yes/partly/no answers per checklist question and the questions you have evidence on file for. Returns a status per step (the four steps of the European Commission Q&A plus being able to show it): unknown, open, partly or measures_reported; the evidence expected per question; the gaps in the file; the actions with priority; and related obligations that are not Article 4 (Articles 26, 27, 50 and 5). No score and no percentage: Article 4 asks for measures, not for a level. Without answers it returns the full checklist. Same rule set as the section on aidoptio.com. Statuses are based only on your own answers: an aid, not legal advice and not proof of meeting the AI Act. Deterministic: no model is called and the answers are not stored.

roles.description: Role groups that work with AI: office, management, hr-sales, board.

ai_uses.description: How AI is used. recruitment-or-hr and credit-or-eligibility make the high-risk questions 4.1 to 4.6 a point to check.

acts_on_its_own.description: true when an AI system acts on its own, for example an agent that sends emails.

is_provider.description: true = provider, false = deployer, left out = not established yet.

high_risk_confirmed.description: true when you have established that the recruitment, HR or credit use is high-risk (Annex III, point 4 or 5). Then questions 4.1 to 4.6 get priority.

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

answers.description: Your own answer per checklist question id, e.g. {"1.1": "yes", "2.4": "partly"}. Call the tool without answers to get the ids and the questions.

evidence_on_file.description: Ids of the questions you have evidence on file for. Leave out to skip the file check (dossier_gaps is then null).

tools.name: estimate_engagement
tools.description: Prices a route of 1 to 5 Aidoptio offers with the published amounts only (EUR, excl. VAT): per step the price model (fixed, from, range, on-request, free), amount or bounds, unit and the page URL; the one credit rule the site states (the full Readiness Sprint fee is credited against Pilot to Production when both are in the route, Sprint first); totals per one-time, per month and per year, where max is null when a step has only a starting price or is quoted per scope. Not a quote: the final amount follows from a written proposal. Example: route ["readiness-sprint"] answers "what does a sprint cost". Rule-based, no model, nothing stored.

route.description: Offer ids in the order of the steps, 1 to 5 (e.g. ["readiness-sprint", "pilot-to-production"]). Ids: get_catalog (services, their tiers and products).

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: prepare_intake_link
tools.description: Returns a link to the Aidoptio contact form (English or Dutch) that fills in the chosen offer, optionally the route of estimate_engagement, a plan hash from plan_vendor_evaluation, benchmark_readiness, ai_act_triage or ai_literacy_scan, and three preferred intake moments. The link carries no name, e-mail or other personal data: the person opens it, adds their own details, checks everything and presses Send (with moments: Confirm these moments, through the booking path without any third-party calendar). This tool sends nothing, books nothing and stores nothing; Aidoptio only receives the request after that click. Also returns the exact message text the form will show.

service.description: Offer id the request is about, e.g. "readiness-sprint".

route.description: Optional route of offers (must contain service), as given to estimate_engagement.

plan_hash.description: Optional 64-character hash from the result of plan_tool (for plan_vendor_evaluation: preregistration.method_hash). Needs plan_tool.

plan_tool.description: The tool that produced plan_hash. Needs plan_hash.

slots.description: Exactly 3 preferred moments for the free 30-minute intake, each {date: YYYY-MM-DD, part: morning (9-12) or afternoon (13-17)}, on different business days or parts, from tomorrow up to 60 days ahead, Europe/Amsterdam time. Optional; ask the person, never guess. The person sees them filled in and confirms them on the site; nothing is booked by this tool.

lang.description: Language of the returned text: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).
